title: Promise and Tide
premise: Petra Eastwick, once the most promising cellist of his generation, walked off stage mid-concert and retreated to the fog-bound fishing town of Greywater Bay, teaching music and keeping his heart as disciplined as his scales. When a record-breaking snowstorm traps him with Callum Reyes—the rival who beat him for the position that broke him, now fleeing his own scandal—the two men are forced into three days of enforced honesty in a shuttered lighthouse inn. As the storm thaws, so does the truth about the sabotage that ended Petra's career, and Callum must decide whether to expose the conductor who ruined them both, risking everything, or protect his own fragile comeback. Petra must finally choose between the safe invisibility he built and a life performed out loud; they end not with a triumphant return to the stage, but with a small, unafraid duet played for one town that truly sees them.
about_author: Freya Fairweather is the pen name of a former orchestral librarian who spent a decade touring coastal towns before turning to fiction full-time. She writes love stories set against weather, water, and second chances from her home on the northern coast.

chapters.title: The Silence After
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Three years after walking off stage mid-concert, Petra teaches cello in Greywater Bay, rigidly scheduled and emotionally walled off. A letter arrives announcing a festival audition that could revive his career. Beat: the cost of safety established.

chapters.title: Salt and Rosin
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Daily routines: students, the harbor café, avoiding the town's curiosity about his past. He practices the audition piece alone at night, hands shaking. Beat: longing disguised as discipline.

chapters.title: The Stranger at the Dock
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Callum Reyes arrives in town incognito, hiding from a scandal involving falsified reviews, planning to lie low at the lighthouse inn. He recognizes Petra instantly. Beat: collision course set.

chapters.title: Old Scores
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra discovers Callum at the café; old humiliation resurfaces—Callum won the seat Petra lost. They exchange barbed courtesies while the sky turns the color of bruise. Beat: rivalry rekindled, attraction flickering beneath it.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The forecast snowstorm becomes a whiteout; roads close, ferries stop, power flickers. Petra's car slides into a drift near the lighthouse inn; Callum pulls him out. Beat: forced proximity begins.

chapters.title: Three Days of Weather
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Stranded together with the innkeeper Marisol, they share meals, arguments, and a battered piano. Callum hears Petra play for the first time since the disaster. Beat: admiration breaking through resentment.

chapters.title: What the Storm Confesses
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Wine loosens Callum; he admits the scandal—that he covered for their former conductor Aldous Vane's review fraud years ago. He doesn't yet confess what he knows about Petra's final concert. Beat: guilt introduced.

chapters.title: The Best Mistake
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A candlelit night, an argument that turns into a kiss, and a night neither can take back. Morning brings panic: Petra retreats into cold formality. Beat: intimacy and immediate retreat.

chapters.title: Thaw
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Roads reopen; Callum prepares to leave. Petra rebuilds his walls, insisting the heart is trainable. But his playing has changed—looser, more alive—and his students notice. Beat: denial cracking.

chapters.title: The Audition Letter
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Callum learns Petra never knew why he lost the principal seat: Vane blackmailed the committee using fabricated evidence about Petra's 'instability.' Callum holds proof. Beat: moral stakes sharpened.

chapters.title: Invisible No More
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Town gossip links Petra to Callum's scandal; a journalist arrives sniffing around both men. Petra's carefully hidden life begins collapsing publicly. Beat: exposure threat rises.

chapters.title: Marisol's Lighthouse
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV (interlude). The innkeeper, herself once disgraced out of a maritime career, watches the two men circle each other and quietly engineers a dinner where truths surface halfway. Beat: wisdom and catalyst.

chapters.title: Half-Truths
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. At dinner, Callum almost tells Petra about Vane's sabotage but stops, terrified of losing him and of destroying his own career by testifying. Petra reads the hesitation as rejection. Beat: miscommunication deepens wound.

chapters.title: The Trainable Heart
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra throws himself into audition prep, treating feeling like a technical problem. His mentor's old recording surfaces, reminding him why he loved music before it hurt him. Beat: false resolution.

chapters.title: Vane's Shadow
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Vane contacts Callum directly, offering career salvation in exchange for silence—and demanding Callum discredit Petra publicly if asked. Callum realizes staying silent makes him complicit forever. Beat: point of no return approaching.

chapters.title: What You Were Never Told
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Callum tells Petra everything: the blackmail, the forged psychiatric report, his own years of silence. Petra's fury is total—not at Vane, but at Callum's cowardice. Beat: rupture; lowest point.

chapters.title: Broken Strings
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra smashes nothing but himself—skips the audition deadline day, drinks, walks the frozen shore. Marisol confronts him: justice outside the law requires showing up. Beat: grief transmuting into resolve.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Callum submits evidence to the festival board and press, sacrificing his own position and comeback. He does it without asking forgiveness first. Beat: sacrifice as climax approach.

chapters.title: The Room Where It Happened
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Public hearing: Vane exposed, records corrected, Petra's name cleared retroactively. Petra attends unannounced and speaks—not about vengeance, but about what music costs when institutions fail artists. Beat: climax; justice achieved at real price.

chapters.title: Running Out of Tide
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Callum, jobless and leaving town, doesn't say goodbye. Petra realizes visibility means chasing, not waiting—he drives through the night to the ferry terminal. Beat: choice made.

chapters.title: Duet
chapters.summary: Both POVs. On the empty winter dock, Petra plays the audition piece aloud, unrehearsed, for an audience of one. Callum stays. They choose each other over careers as armor. Beat: emotional resolution.

chapters.title: Promise and Tide
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Petra's POV. One year later: no orchestra podium, but a thriving community music school in Greywater Bay co-founded with Callum, and a small honest life. Final image: two cellos, one open door, tide coming in. Beat: belonging earned.
